title: Reject stale daemon approval commands
description: Objective: implement compare-and-swap approval against the durable planRevision producer task-492b573920264188888d56638dd98d81; work only after its delivered contract is available. Deliverable: optional expectedPlanRevision forwarded by StateManager.approveTask to taskStore.approveTask, plus APPROVE_TASK and the UPDATE_TASK AWAITING_APPROVAL-to-WORKING route in WebSocketServer. Put UPDATE_TASK command metadata beside taskId/updates, never persist it; strip forged planRevision and expectedPlanRevision from updates. Under the existing state mutex, validate supplied revision then compare to current effective revision before cancelSpeedModeTimeout or any write/publication. Only absence uses legacy approval; null, strings, booleans, fractional/negative/unsafe/non-finite numbers refuse INVALID_INPUT. A mismatch throws MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT (-32002) with codeName PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH and safe taskId/expected/current revision details. WS ERROR keeps existing message, operation, context.taskId plus machine-readable code/codeName and allowlisted revision details, never arbitrary exception contexts. Use existing registration census to confirm no MCP approve_task tool exists; do not create one or repurpose set_task_status, whose role/policy stays unchanged. Scope: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts, src/state/StateManager.ts, src/server/WebSocketServer.ts, new src/server/planApproval.test.ts, docs/MCP_SERVER.md (5 files). Tests use real serialization/dispatch or explicitly state.runExclusive, not concurrent direct handlers that bypass production locking. NOT in scope: IDE rendering, in-place revision policy, SPEED/TURBO policy rewrites, Wave 1. Verification at repo root: npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test (Windows npm.cmd); document wire contract where no MCP approval tool exists. Capture focused old-behavior failure.
definitionOfDone: Vitest proves current revision approves with PLAN_APPROVED and planApprovedAt; omitted revision remains accepted; legacy task without a stored revision accepts explicit 0.

Stale revision throws/returns exact STATE_CONFLICT code -32002 and PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH codeName; task remains AWAITING_APPROVAL with persisted bytes, map, timestamps, assignment, activity/events and pending SPEED timeout unchanged.

Malformed supplied tokens refuse INVALID_INPUT instead of coercion or legacy fallback; unrelated error responses retain backwards-compatible message/operation fields and do not leak unallowlisted context.
Both APPROVE_TASK and UPDATE_TASK approval routes forward the token under the mutex; forged stored stamps and command metadata are not writable task fields, proven by WS regression tests.
A serialized newer-submit-before-older-approval race rejects the older token; a matched/legacy approval still succeeds under existing policy, proven through the real dispatch/locking path.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md records the actual approval wire/error shape and absence of MCP approve_task; fresh npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test exits 0 with nonzero counts and recorded red proof.
taskRails: Compare before timer cancellation or task mutation; do not weaken status/role checks.
A task-write failure does not promise new multi-entity transaction rollback.
No new MCP approval tool or automatic approval policy change.

implementationPlan.description: IMPLEMENT THE COMPARE-AND-SWAP IN THE STORE AND FORWARD IT THROUGH THE FACADE. In taskStore.ts add an exported-or-local validator `decodeSuppliedPlanRevision(value: unknown, taskId: string): number` that accepts only `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 0`; everything else (null, strings, booleans, fractional, negative, unsafe, non-finite) throws `invalidInput('expectedPlanRevision', ...)` — no coercion, no legacy fallback. This is the whole error handling contract for a supplied token. Change the signature to `approveTask(state, taskId, expectedPlanRevision?: unknown)`; type it `unknown`, not `number`, so an untyped WS payload cannot bypass validation. Order inside the function is load-bearing and must be: existing task lookup, existing AWAITING_APPROVAL status check (do not weaken either), then — only when `expectedPlanRevision !== undefined` — validate the supplied token, read the current effective revision with the existing `decodeStoredPlanRevision(task)` (absent stamp reads as 0, so a legacy row matches explicit 0, and a corrupt stored stamp still fails closed as INVALID_INPUT), and on `supplied !== current` throw `new MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, <message naming the task and both revisions>, { taskId, expectedPlanRevision: supplied, currentPlanRevision: current }, 'PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH')`. Every one of those throws must happen BEFORE `cancelSpeedModeTimeout(taskId)` and before `state.updateTask(...)`, so a refusal cancels no timer and writes nothing. An absent token skips the block entirely and takes the unchanged legacy path. Keep the existing comment about callers holding the mutex. In StateManager.ts widen the facade at line 625 to `approveTask(taskId: string, expectedPlanRevision?: unknown)` and forward the third argument verbatim. Do not add a new cross-entity transaction or rollback promise. Re-run the focused test file; groups A-G must now pass.
implementationPlan.note:
Store-level compare-and-swap landed plus the facade forward. Two files, no new dependency, no new transaction.

taskStore.ts: added the local validator `decodeSuppliedPlanRevision(value: unknown, taskId: string): number` beside the existing `decodeStoredPlanRevision`. It accepts only `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= 0`; everything else throws `invalidInput('expectedPlanRevision', ...)`. Number.isSafeInteger already rejects NaN, Infinity and fractional values, so no separate finite check and no Number() anywhere — a coercion would reintroduce exactly the bug. The thrown message tells the caller to OMIT the field for a token-free approval, which is the only legacy opt-out.

`approveTask` is now `(state, taskId, expectedPlanRevision?: unknown)` — `unknown`, not `number`, so an untyped WS payload cannot bypass validation by type-assertion at the call site. Order inside is load-bearing and is: getTask, the unchanged AWAITING_APPROVAL check, then the new `if (expectedPlanRevision !== undefined)` block (validate the token, read the effective current revision via decodeStoredPlanRevision so an absent stamp reads 0 and a corrupt stamp still fails closed as INVALID_INPUT, then throw MoeError STATE_CONFLICT with codeName PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH and context { taskId, expectedPlanRevision, currentPlanRevision } when they differ), and only after all of that the original cancelSpeedModeTimeout + updateTask. Comparison is `!==`, not `<`: a newer token is stale-or-forged too. The mutex comment is unchanged. An absent token skips the block entirely, so the existing legacy path is byte-for-byte the old one.

In the UPDATE_TASK case capture the raw token from the payload (NOT from `updates`, which is already stripped) before entering the mutex, and pass it at the AWAITING_APPROVAL->WORKING delegation around line 404: `return this.state.approveTask(taskId, approvalToken)`. Omission of the key over the wire is the only legacy opt-out; an explicit JSON null is a malformed token and must surface INVALID_INPUT. APPROVE_TASK forwards `message.payload.expectedPlanRevision` as the second argument to state.approveTask INSIDE the existing withMutex call, so validation and comparison are serialized with the status re-check and the write.

UPDATE_TASK destructures the token out of the PAYLOAD as `approvalToken` (`const { taskId, updates, expectedPlanRevision: approvalToken } = message.payload`) before the safeUpdates strip and before the mutex, then passes it at the AWAITING_APPROVAL to WORKING delegation: `return this.state.approveTask(taskId, approvalToken)`. Reading it from the payload rather than from `updates` is the point — `updates` is already denylist-stripped, so a client cannot supply its own token there. The route still deliberately ignores the rest of safeUpdates; that behavior was not extended.

Key omission is the only legacy opt-out because JSON cannot carry undefined; an explicit null arrives as null and reaches the store validator, which refuses it as INVALID_INPUT.

implementationPlan.description: MAKE THE ERROR FRAME MACHINE-READABLE WITHOUT LEAKING CONTEXT. WebSocketServer.ts does not import from util/errors.js yet — add `import { MoeError } from '../util/errors.js'`. In the single catch-all ERROR builder (around lines 945-960) keep `type`, `message` and `operation` exactly as they are and keep `context.taskId` / `context.epicId` exactly as they are, so every unrelated error response stays backwards compatible. Additively: when the caught value is a MoeError, add top-level `code` (the numeric MoeErrorCode, -32002 for a mismatch) and `codeName` (the stable string, 'PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH' or 'INVALID_INPUT'). Never spread `error.context` — write a small module-local pure helper that reads at most the two allowlisted keys `expectedPlanRevision` and `currentPlanRevision` from `error.context`, emits each only when it is a finite number, and merges them into the existing `context` object beside taskId. A non-MoeError (a plain Error from a transition check, for example) must gain neither `code` nor `codeName` and no extra context keys — that is the error handling regression the test asserts. Re-run the focused test file; every group including the allowlist and the no-leak assertions must pass.

ERROR frame is machine-readable and leak-proof. Focused file is fully GREEN: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 30 passed (30), EXIT=0. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` also exits 0.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review done against the full diff (`git diff 58e0546`). No code changed in this step; one factual correction to a plan premise is recorded below. Every checklist item confirmed:

ORDERING. taskStore.approveTask runs getTask, then the untouched AWAITING_APPROVAL status check, then the CAS block, and only then cancelSpeedModeTimeout + state.updateTask. Both throws (INVALID_INPUT and STATE_CONFLICT) are inside the CAS block, so a refusal cancels no timer, writes no bytes and publishes nothing (updateTask is the only publisher). Proven behaviorally, not by reading: the SPEED group arms a real timer, refuses a stale approval, then lets the timer fire and observes PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED.

VALIDATION NOT COERCION. decodeSuppliedPlanRevision rejects anything that is not `typeof 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger && >= 0`. No Number() anywhere in the path. A malformed token throws instead of degrading into the legacy approval.

ABSENCE VS NULL. `expectedPlanRevision !== undefined` gates the whole block, so omission skips it entirely while an explicit null enters it and fails decode. Genuinely different code paths.

FORGERY. Unreachable through three independent layers: WebSocketServer strips both `planRevision` and `expectedPlanRevision` from `updates` via UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST; taskStore.updateTask strips `planRevision` again at line 221; and the approval route ignores safeUpdates wholesale, so nothing from `updates` reaches disk there at all. I also checked the creation route, which the plan did not name: createTask builds its Task literal field-by-field with no input spread and hardcodes `planRevision: 0` with a comment saying it ignores whatever the caller passed, so CREATE_TASK cannot seed a forged stamp either.

ERROR ALLOWLIST. The builder never spreads error.context. allowlistedErrorContext iterates a frozen two-key const list and emits a key only when the value is a finite number, so an unrelated MoeError carrying field/reason/entity/id/paths forwards nothing; `__proto__` is not in the list. code/codeName are added only for a MoeError, so a plain Error (the illegal-transition check) keeps the byte-identical legacy frame.

TOKEN-FREE CALLERS — PLAN PREMISE CORRECTED. The plan and the architect's notes said submitPlan.ts SPEED/TURBO auto-approval and setTaskStatus.ts relaxed-mode approval are approveTask callers that must keep working. They are NOT. A full census of `approveTask(` across src shows submitPlan.ts calls `state.updateTask(..., 'PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED')` directly (lines 59 and 391) and setTaskStatus.ts sets planApprovedAt + emits PLAN_APPROVED through its own updates object (lines 233-242). Neither ever reached the store helper, so neither could have broken, and neither is fenced by this CAS — which is correct, because they are daemon-owned policy paths with no client-supplied token. The real token-free callers are three test sites: StateManager.test.ts:730/735, taskTimestamps.test.ts:44 and __e2e__/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts:93. All four call sites pass unchanged in the green suite. This strengthens rather than weakens the documented limitation and I have stated it plainly for QA.

NOT WEAKENED / NOT ADDED. The status check is untouched and still runs before the CAS; no role check was modified; no MCP approval tool exists (`grep approve_task src/tools/index.ts` returns nothing, and registry.test.ts asserts every exported *Tool factory is registered, so absence is real); no new cross-entity transaction or rollback promise was introduced.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A new moe.approve_task MCP tool carrying the token — rejected: the registration census shows no such tool and a task rail forbids adding one; approval is human-gated over /ws. (2) Putting expectedPlanRevision inside UPDATE_TASK.updates — rejected: updates flow into taskStore.updateTask and would make the token a writable task field, which is exactly the forgery hole; it goes beside taskId/updates as command metadata and both key names are added to the denylist. (3) Validating the token in WebSocketServer and passing a clean number down — rejected: two WS routes plus future callers would each need the same validation; typing the store parameter `unknown` and validating once in taskStore keeps a single authority and lets TypeScript refuse a caller that tries to skip it. (4) Comparing with < so only older tokens refuse — rejected: any non-equal token is stale-or-forged; a dedicated N+1 test kills that mutant. (5) Proving the SPEED timer survived by spying on cancelSpeedModeTimeout — usable, but the stronger proof is behavioral: arm a real SPEED timer, refuse a stale approval, then let the timer fire and observe PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Slice 1 (commit 7da080b) already landed the producer: optional Task.planRevision in types/schema.ts and, in taskStore.ts around lines 40-130, MAX_PLAN_REVISION / decodeStoredPlanRevision / derivePlanRevision. decodeStoredPlanRevision is the right read for the current effective revision — absent reads as 0 (so a legacy row matches explicit 0) and a corrupt stamp throws INVALID_INPUT, failing closed. util/errors.ts MoeError takes an explicit 4th codeName argument, so PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH needs no enum edit; MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT is already -32002 and INVALID_INPUT is -32602. taskStore.approveTask (line 428) documents that callers hold the mutex and it does not acquire it; WebSocketServer.withMutex is state.runExclusive, so both WS routes are already serialized. The UPDATE_TASK approval route at line 404 delegates to state.approveTask and deliberately discards the rest of safeUpdates — preserve that. WebSocketServer.ts has a single catch-all ERROR builder near line 945 that already emits message/operation/context.taskId, and it does NOT yet import from util/errors.js. Three callers approve with no token today and must keep working: submitPlan.ts SPEED and TURBO auto-approval, setTaskStatus.ts relaxed-mode plan approval, and taskTimestamps.test.ts. WebSocketServer.test.ts has the exact real-socket harness to copy (temp .moe, port 0, connectAndCollect); toolTestHarness.ts in src/tools is available for seeding. StateManager.load uses raw loadEntities, so a task JSON written without planRevision is a faithful legacy row.
planningNotes.risks: Ordering is the whole feature: any validation or comparison placed after cancelSpeedModeTimeout silently kills a pending SPEED timer on a refused approval — assert it behaviorally, not by reading the code. Number.isSafeInteger already rejects NaN, Infinity and fractional values, but a bare `typeof === 'number'` check would let them through, and `Number(value)` anywhere in this path reintroduces coercion. JSON cannot carry undefined, so key omission is the only legacy signal on the wire while an explicit null must refuse — test both. Spreading error.context into the ERROR frame would leak field/reason and paths from unrelated MoeErrors; only the two revision keys may cross. speedModeTimeouts is module-private, so a test that arms a real SPEED timer must call the exported clearAllSpeedModeTimeouts in afterEach or it leaks into sibling files. Vitest output here is buried in pino logs and a filtered pipeline hides the exit code — capture the code separately. tsconfig excludes test files, so tsc will not type-check the new one. Do not widen into IDE rendering, in-place revision policy, SPEED/TURBO policy or Wave 1, and do not claim a universal stale-approval fence: a SPEED callback already queued behind the mutex can still auto-approve after a human refusal, and that limitation belongs in the completion summary.
